caseno: Appeal from Original Order No 57 of 1976.
lawyer: Sk. Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury for Farmanullah Khan, Advocates ----- For the Appellants.
parties:
Amina Khatun & others ----- Appellant
Vs.
M/s. Quickways Agency ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
2. The appellants filed Miscellaneous Judicial (WC) Case No. 20 of 1969 under section 10 of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 claiming Rs. 6000/- on the allegations, inter alia, that they were heirs of one Manu Mia, a labourer in the Chittagong Jetty, under the opposite party M/s Quickways Agency. The said Manu Mia made an accident and sustained injuries while he was loading cargo of M/s. Barkat Ali at Jetty No. 7 on January 7, 1967. As a result of the accident there was compound fracture with dislocation of left ankle with gangrene and tetanus. He died as a result of such injury in the Chittagong Medical Hospital on February 8, 1967. The opposite party was aware about the accident and death of Manu Mia and the representatives of the opposite party paid Rs. 200/- to the petitioners with a promise to pay further Rs. 6000/- on behalf of the opposite party. 

 3. The said case was resisted by the opposite party on various grounds. It was alleged that there was no relationship of employer and employees between the opposite party and the deceased Manu Mia, the opposite party did not receive any notice of accident and death of Manu Mia, the opposite party never paid any sum nor did they promise to pay Rs. 6000/-, the claim of the petitioners is barred by limitation, the Miscellaneous Case under section 10 of the Act suffered from defect of parties as the contractor of the opposite party and the owner of the cargo who were necessary parties had not been impleaded in this case, Manu Mia was a casual labour on the daily wages basis and the accident did not take place in the business area of the opposite party. 

 In this case the applicants did not satisfy the requirement of the aforesaid provision of law as they failed to prove that Manu Mia was employed as a workman under the opposite party M/s Quickways Agency in that the Register of the said opposite party maintained containing the name of workmen does not include the name of Manu Mia. Although in the case of Aftab Flur and Allied Industries Ltd. Vs. Mst. Nasim Akhtar, 16 DLR (WP) 199, it has been held that a workman includes a casual worker. But in this case there being no evidence on record that Manu Mia was a casual worker the Commissioner rightly found that Manu Mia was not a casual worker and there was no relationship of master and servant between the employer and Manu Miah. The Commissioner also found that the claim was barred by limitation and as such no award for compensation can be allowed. The learned Advocate submits that the Commissioner committed an error of law in holding that the case is barred by limitation but he was unable to point out before me any defect as to the finding of limitation. He submits that the notice under section 11 having been sent through Dock Labourer of Chittagong Jetty No. 6 there was sufficient compliance and the Commissioner wrongly held that there being violation of this mandatory provision a claim cannot be allowed. Section 11 enjoins service of notice upon the employer and not upon any other person and worker sustaining the injury caused as a result of accident shall submit himself for medical examination by a qualified doctor of the employer. In this appeal I do not find that there was any evidence on record to show that the requirements of section 11 of the Act were satisfied. In that view of the matter the contention of the learned Advocate is of no substance. In view of the findings of the Commissioner the learned Advocate fails to make out a case of "a substantial question of law" in the appeal. Where an order of Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation does not involve "a substantial question of law" no appeal under section 30 of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 lies. In the instant case, as no such question of law emerges from the order appealed this appeal is not maintainable in view of the first proviso to section 30 of the Act. There is no substance in this appeal.
